title: CLO 2025.0 - Scope Dragging
description: Starting from version 2025.0, when clicking and dragging clothing in simulation mode, it is possible to define the dragged area and intensity, allowing precise adjustments according to requirements. This enables the creation of more realistic folds and shapes in the clothing.
transcript:
This video introduces the range pull function for you.  
Starting from the 2025 version, when you press and pull the clothing in simulation mode,  
the area and strength of the pull support are defined, and precise adjustments are made according to the needs.  
Now it shows several application scenarios for range pull.  
For single-layer clothing, we can create small-range twist details through the range pull function.  
You can also make relatively large-range adjustments to the back of a suit.  
When modifying posture, you can use the range pull to adjust the waist with a multi-layer structure.  
Next, let's take a look at how to use it.  
To use the range pull, we need to open the simulation first.  
Once the simulation is opened, select the move tool to switch to the small-handle point pull tool.  
At this time, press and hold the point pull tool for two seconds, and we can see the tool group.  
Press the range pull tool and move the mouse to the 3D window of the clothing.  
You can see that on the basis of the original grip, two new circles have been added.  
This is our range brush.  
It can help you directly understand the range of influence of the range pull.  
In addition, we can also see that there is a range pull window setting.  
The window setting is divided into two main parts: range and options.  
First, let's look at the range.  
The reduction type below the range is controlled by the shape of the pull effect.  
You can switch it to a curve or a straight line.  
The range of soft selection and the degree of reduction separately control the range of influence when the pull is pulled and the range of the center point.  
The smaller inner circle of the two circles indicates the area where the pull effect is most directly applied.  
As the effect radiates outward, the strength gradually decreases, resulting in a smooth, natural reduction.  
The range of soft selection controls the area affected by the pull.  
As the value increases, the size of the two circles on the clothing will also expand accordingly.  
The default value is 200, and it can be adjusted within the range of 1 to 500.  
The degree of reduction is controlled from the core area of the pull to the maximum range of influence.  
The default value is 0, and it can be adjusted within the range of -2 to 2.  
The chart area below can help you understand more objectively.  
When the reduction type is a curve, the pull selection area is not a single pull, but a smoother, rounder, and wider shape.  
Next, let's use the curve as an example to see the effect.  
Let's use the default value of the pull sleeve first.  
Change the soft selection range to 250.  
Turn to the back of the suit to pull.  
You will see that the pull effect is more effective in the area where the same core is defined.  
This time, let's set the soft selection range to 500 and pull the clothing.  
Compared to before, the area covered by the inner circle and the outer circle is now twice as wide.  
You can pull a larger area.  
Now let's set the value to be the smallest.  
Then pull the panel again.  
The soft selection range is only 1 mm.  
This allows us to make a very small range of pull.  
Next, we will change the soft selection range to 200.  
And set the degree of reduction to the smallest value of -2.  
Then pull.  
In this case, the inner circle almost overlaps with the outer circle.  
The pull effect is evenly distributed in a larger area, rather than concentrated on a specific point.  
Finally, let's set the maximum value to 2 and pull the clothes again.  
Through the chart below, you can see that the pull force is highly concentrated at a specific point.  
This means that precise operation is performed in small areas.  
Next, we will adjust the degree of reduction to 1.  
The reduction type is modified to a straight line.  
The straight line allows you to define a smaller and more detailed core area to be squeezed.  
After switching to the straight line option, you will notice that the image becomes sharper and sharper.  
At this time, when you pull the clothes, you will find that the selection range of the core area is narrower and more accurate than the curve line.  
So you can control the pull correctly.  
You can choose the reduction type according to your preferences.  
Next, let's take a look at how to display and control the pull selection area.  
At the bottom of the options, the range measurement method defines how to calculate the selection area from the actual point.  
It is divided into two types: surface and straight line.  
In surface mode, the pull effect is only applicable to the surface of a selected layer within the specified range.  
Even if there are multiple layers here, it is the same.  
However, when the pull and the strip are sewn together, any soft selection range that is defined and the area within the reduction range will be affected simultaneously.  
The straight line option allows you to pull all the sheets within a certain distance.  
Whether the selected sheet is sewn together with the sheets of other layers,  
when you use this option to pull the sheet, you will see that all the sheets within the defined range are affected at the same time.  
The range brush display can help you understand the range of the pull function more objectively.  
You can also turn off the range brush display here.  
Now let's take a look at the use of each range measurement method.  
The range brush display is only used for the effect of pulling the area when selecting the selected sheet.  
As you can see, whether it is surface or straight line,  
as a range measurement method and only used for selecting the selected sheet,  
when the range brush is turned on, it will only affect the currently selected sheet.  
When you want to pull a specific sheet in the given work process,  
no matter which range measurement method you choose, this option is very useful.  
Next, when the full weight function is used,  
the range brush display will show the pull area in green.  
If you turn off this option, the range brush display will no longer show the area in green,  
but it will not affect the effect of the range brush.  
The range brush is not only used to adjust the overall effect of the clothes,  
but it can also help quickly adjust various details such as knotting and tying.  
First, re-position the fixed pin and prepare for the knotting.  
Then select the range brush tool and adjust the range and degree of reduction according to the brush size.  
After the setting is complete, turn to the appropriate angle,  
pull the clothes to complete the knotting details.  
After achieving the desired effect, delete the fixed pin and continue to simulate.  
Then the introduction of the range brush function is here.  
I hope this function can help you quickly adjust the ideal clothing effect.

chunks.content: # CLO 2025.0 - Scope Dragging (Range Pull) This document explains the range pull function introduced in CLO 2025.0, covering its usage, settings, and application scenarios for precise garment simulation adjustments. Key terms include range pull, soft selection, reduction type, range brush, and range measurement methods. --- ## Introduction to Range Pull Function The range pull function in CLO 2025.0 allows users to press and pull clothing in simulation mode with defined area and strength of pull influence. This enables detailed, precise adjustments for clothing simulations, adapting pull effects based on user needs. ### Application Scenarios - **Single-layer clothing:** Create small-range twist details. - **Large-range adjustments:** Modify areas like the back of a suit. - **Multi-layer structures:** Adjust posture-related areas such as the waist. --- ## How to Use Range Pull This section details how to activate and operate the range pull tool in CLO 2025.0. 1. **Open Simulation Mode:** Begin by opening the simulation. 2. **Select Move Tool:** Switch to the small-handle point pull tool. 3. **Access Range Pull Tool:** Press and hold the point pull tool for two seconds to open the tool group, then select the range pull tool. 4. **Range Brush Visualization:** Two new circles appear on the garment indicating the range brush, which visually defines the pull influence area. --- ## Range Pull Window Settings The range pull window is divided into two main sections: **Range** and **Options**. ### Range Settings - **Reduction Type:** Controls the shape of the pull effect; can be set to *curve* or *straight line*. - **Soft Selection Range:** Controls the size of the pull influence area, indicated by two circles on the garment. The inner circle represents the core area of strongest pull effect, and the outer circle marks the maximum influence radius. - Default: 200 - Range: 1 to 500 - **Degree of Reduction:** Controls how the pull strength decreases from the core to the outer range. - Default: 0 - Range: -2 to 2 A chart visualizes how the pull strength reduces across the selected range. --- ## Using Reduction Types and Parameter Effects ### Curve Reduction Type - Produces a smooth, round, and wide pull influence. - Increasing soft selection range enlarges both inner and outer circles, allowing larger areas to be pulled. - Example: - Soft selection range 250: Moderate pull area on back of suit. - Soft selection range 500: Twice as large pull area compared to 250. - Soft selection range 1: Extremely small pull area for fine control. - Degree of reduction affects distribution: - At -2, the inner and outer circles nearly overlap, distributing pull evenly over a larger area. - At 2, pull force is highly concentrated in a small core area for precise small-area adjustments. ### Straight Line Reduction Type - Creates a sharper, narrower core area for more detailed control. - The image of the pull area becomes sharper, and the core selection range is more precise than with the curve option.

chunks.content: - Degree of reduction affects distribution: - At -2, the inner and outer circles nearly overlap, distributing pull evenly over a larger area. - At 2, pull force is highly concentrated in a small core area for precise small-area adjustments. ### Straight Line Reduction Type - Creates a sharper, narrower core area for more detailed control. - The image of the pull area becomes sharper, and the core selection range is more precise than with the curve option. - Suitable for users who desire more focused manipulation of the garment. --- ## Range Measurement Methods Defines how the pull selection area is calculated from the point of interaction. 1. **Surface Mode:** - Pull effect applies only to the surface of the selected layer within the specified range. - Even with multiple layers, only the selected sheet's surface is affected. - When layers are sewn together, overlapping soft selection ranges affect connected areas simultaneously. 2. **Straight Line Mode:** - Pull effect applies to all sheets within a certain linear distance. - All sheets within range are affected simultaneously, regardless of sewing connections. --- ## Range Brush Display and Control - The range brush visually represents the pull influence area on the garment. - Can be toggled on or off in the options. - When active, it only affects the currently selected sheet, useful for precise sheet-specific edits. - When the full weight function is enabled, the range brush area appears green; disabling this does not affect pull function, only the visual indicator. - Useful for quickly understanding and controlling the pull range during detailed garment work. --- ## Practical Use Cases for Range Pull ### Detail Adjustments (Knotting and Tying) 1. Re-position fixed pins to prepare the garment. 2. Select the range brush tool and adjust the soft selection range and degree of reduction to match the intended brush size. 3. Rotate the garment to a suitable angle. 4. Pull the clothing to create knotting or tying details. 5. Remove fixed pins after achieving the desired effect and continue simulation. --- ## Summary The range pull function in CLO 2025.0 offers enhanced control over garment simulation by defining the area and strength of pull influence through adjustable parameters such as soft selection range, degree of reduction, reduction type (curve or straight line), and range measurement method (surface or straight line). The range brush provides a visual guide to the effective pull region, enabling both broad and fine adjustments. This tool is especially useful for detailed garment effects like twisting, knotting, and posture modifications across single or multiple clothing layers.
